ev.q: In 2009, an estimated 210,830 nonfatal occupational injuries and illnesses among older workers resulted in lost workdays
Rates were calculated per 10,000 full-time equivalent (FTE) workers (one FTE = 2,000 hours worked per year)
had a rate of nonfatal occupational injuries and illnesses resulting in lost workdays of 116.8 per 10,000 FTE workers
Fractures accounted for 11% of all injuries among workers aged ≥55 years
had longer absences from work compared with females (medians of 14 and 9 days away from work, respectively)
workers aged ≥65 years had a rate of 105.9 per 10,000 FTE workers
Older workers had higher rates of falls on the same level, fractures, and hip injuries compared with younger workers
an analysis of data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Survey of Occupational Injuries and Illnesses (SOII) was conducted

methods_quotes.q: Rates of nonfatal occupational injuries and illnesses resulting in at least 1 day away from work were calculated using hours of work data
Rates were calculated per 10,000 full-time equivalent (FTE) workers (one FTE = 2,000 hours worked per year); 95% confidence intervals also were calculated
Data do not meet BLS standards for publication.
